# How to Use Amazon's Conversational Alexa+ at Home

Imagine asking your smart speaker to help you organize a busy weekend, suggest dinner recipes, and schedule your day without having to repeat her name every few seconds. This guide will show you how to use the upgraded Alexa+ to have fluid, natural conversations that make managing your home much easier. While Alexa+ can help plan and coordinate tasks, remember it can't physically perform actions like cooking or directly send emails outside of its integrated systems.

## Before you start
- **An Alexa-enabled device:** This guide applies to any compatible Amazon Echo speaker, smart display (like an Echo Show), or the official Alexa app installed on your mobile phone or tablet.
- **An active Amazon account:** Your device needs to be set up and linked to your Amazon account.
- **Alexa+ turned on:** In the US, Alexa+ is available to all customers and is free for Prime members. If you have Prime, say "Alexa, upgrade to Alexa+" to your device, or sign in with your Amazon account at alexa.com. Without Prime, alexa.com and the Alexa app offer a free text-based chat with limited access.
- **A stable internet connection:** Your Alexa device needs a reliable Wi-Fi connection to access its cloud-based AI capabilities.
- **Rough total time:** Allow about 5-10 minutes to follow this guide and try out a short conversation.

## Step 1 — Turn on Follow-Up Mode
Alexa+ is built for natural, back-and-forth conversation and uses **generative AI** (an advanced type of artificial intelligence that can create new, human-like responses and content, acting like a highly capable digital assistant). To keep talking without saying her name every time, you use a setting called Follow-Up Mode. Amazon says you can switch it on by saying "Turn on Follow-Up Mode", or in your device settings or the Alexa app.

You'll know it worked when Alexa confirms the change and, after her next answer, a visual indicator shows that you can speak without the wake word.

💬 Example: Say clearly, "Alexa, turn on Follow-Up Mode."

## Step 2 — Ask for help with a household task
With Alexa+ ready, you can speak to her more naturally, just like you would to a person. You don't need to use stiff commands. Describe your situation or request in detail. Alexa+ is designed to understand **context** (this means she remembers previous parts of your conversation, much like you'd remember what a friend told you moments ago), so feel free to provide background information.

You'll know it worked when Alexa processes your request and starts offering suggestions or asking clarifying questions, showing she's grasped the core of your query.

💬 Example: "I have some leftover roast pumpkin and spinach in the fridge. What is a quick, colorful lunch I can make with these in ten minutes?"

## Step 3 — Refine ideas without repeating yourself
Once Alexa+ offers her initial suggestions, you don't need to say her wake word ("Alexa") again to continue the discussion, as long as Follow-Up Mode is on. According to Amazon, you can follow up for up to about 8 seconds after Alexa's response, and a visual indicator shows when you can speak without the wake word. You can immediately ask to modify a suggestion, request more details, or explore different options.

If the indicator goes away, Alexa has stopped listening for follow-ups. Just say "Alexa" again and continue. Follow-Up Mode does not work in every situation: Amazon notes it is not available during media playback or calls, and it does not apply to skills or smart home commands.

You'll know it worked when Alexa responds directly to your follow-up, building on her previous answer without you needing to say her name.

💬 Example: "That salad sounds great, but I do not have any feta cheese. What can I use instead?"

## Step 4 — Turn your conversation into action
After you've refined your plan and settled on a course of action, you can ask Alexa+ to help you make it happen. For example, you can ask her to add items to your shopping list or to set a reminder or a timer. This saves you from manually performing these common follow-up tasks.

If Alexa says she can't complete an action, try rephrasing your request. For instance, instead of "send this," try "add this to my shopping list."

You'll know it worked when Alexa verbally confirms that she has performed the requested action, for example, "I've added the new ingredients to your shopping list," or "Your cooking timer for fifteen minutes has been set."

💬 Example: "Perfect. Add the alternative ingredients to my shopping list and set a cooking timer for fifteen minutes."

## Step 5 — End the conversation
When you're finished, you can simply stop speaking. The follow-up window only lasts for a few seconds after Alexa's answer, so she returns to her standard "wake word needed" state on her own. If you prefer, you can also say something like "Thank you, Alexa. That's all for now."

If Alexa seems to keep listening after a long pause, you can always turn Follow-Up Mode off by saying "Turn off Follow-Up Mode" or in your device settings or the Alexa app.

You'll know it worked when the follow-up indicator is gone and Alexa only responds again when you say her name.

💬 Example: "Thank you, Alexa. That's all for now."

## Step 6 — Review your actions
It's always a good idea to quickly check that Alexa carried out the tasks you requested, especially for things like shopping lists or reminders. You can ask Alexa directly, or open the Alexa app on your phone to verify. This step helps build confidence in using her conversational abilities for important daily management.

You'll know it worked when Alexa reads back your items, or you see the new items or reminders correctly listed in the Alexa app.

💬 Example: "Alexa, what's on my shopping list?" or "Alexa, what reminders do I have for today?"

## Common mistakes
- **Repeating the wake word unnecessarily:** It's natural to want to say "Alexa" before every sentence, but while the follow-up indicator is showing, you don't need to. The fix: If the indicator is visible, just keep talking.
- **Waiting too long to speak:** The follow-up window only stays open for about 8 seconds after Alexa finishes speaking. If you need a moment to think, she might stop listening. The fix: If you need to pause, try to keep your response relatively quick, or simply say "Alexa" again to continue.
- **Over-complicating your requests:** While Alexa+ is much smarter now, giving ten different, complex instructions in one long breath can still lead to misunderstandings. The fix: Break down complex requests into one or two thoughts at a time, allowing Alexa to process each piece of information before moving on.

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** You can easily organize chaotic family schedules, brainstorm dinner options, or plan your weekend activities entirely hands-free while washing up or cooking, making household management feel less like a chore.
- **For your business or work:** If you work from home, you can use Alexa+ as a quick brainstorming partner to outline your daily schedule, draft a simple checklist for your projects, or get quick facts without breaking your workflow.
- **If you're just getting started:** Keep things light and simple. Start by asking for a straightforward recommendation, like a three-step evening wind-down routine, to get used to the natural flow of the conversation.

## Try it now
Walk up to your Alexa device (or open the Alexa app) and say: **"Alexa, turn on Follow-Up Mode."**

Then ask: **"Can you help me plan a quick morning routine for a productive day?"** See what she suggests, and then try asking one follow-up question, like "What about an evening wind-down routine?" without saying her name again.
